about: Every tool Shepherd registers, where, and the verdict (docs/context-budget.md). keep: sent in every request of the context; defer: registered `deferred` (SHEPHERD_DEFER_TOOLS=1, which the app sets while Settings > Agents > Context > Defer rarely used tools is on), so pi sends none of it until the model loads it with tool_search; drop: not registered there at all, with why. Tests/Extensions/context-budget.test.mjs launches each context on a real pi and fails when a tool it registers has no row, a kept tool is not sent, a deferred one is sent or not registered, or a dropped one is back. The groups are what the Context card's system-prompt breakdown calls them (ContextToolGroups).

families.reason: pi's own: what an agent does with a repository.

Pi's native script executor, hosted by the status extension while codemode is enabled (on by default). Its definition costs 269 tokens and its prompt guidance ~600 more, for a tool a minority of turns use, so it is deferred with the rest (tool_search loads it when a script is the way; a design's agent, which has no tool_search, keeps it direct). Direct model APIs are disabled, with a five-minute deadline and 128 tool calls per script. Native subagents do not load the status extension.

The one way a thread reaches the person: its question goes through pi's native dialog to the question dock and Needs you on every device. Kept direct (about 150 tokens): a model that has to search for it asks in prose instead. An automation run has nobody watching and a native subagent asks its parent, so neither loads it.
The thread's terminal tabs (command-J) are how an agent runs a dev server or a watcher; six small tools, 590 tokens together.

User-requested local project management is rare. Reuse live state, not cached projects.json. Edits are metadata-only unless folder transfer is explicit; removal requires confirmation. No project-management tools in automation runs.

Reaching other threads is something the user asks for, and each description says so first (agent-to-agent messages). Deferred: 1.4k tokens of definitions and 65 of tool-list lines out of every request. The prompt names agent_* and says it is only when the user explicitly asks, and the rule about a message that arrives from another agent stays in it whether or not they are loaded.

Messaging another thread is the user's call in a thread (deferred with the rest of agent_*). An automation's run reports completion to the thread that made it with it, the only agent tool a run gets, so it stays direct there.
Managing automations is rare: 0.8k tokens of definitions and 85 of tool-list lines. A run's own agent never gets them (an automation cannot start automations).
One small tool (105 tokens) an unattended run needs to say it finished, so it stays direct; deferring it would save a thread 118 tokens and cost a search in every run.

Readies the side pane's Changes tab: 245 tokens and a tool-list line for something a thread does now and then. Deferred in a thread and an automation; a design's agent never gets it (its screen has no Changes tab and its folder is no repository).

Delegating to a helper is how a thread keeps a big search out of its own context (docs/context-budget.md, For agents), so starting one, messaging it, reading its result and answering its question (shepherd_child_resume with the questionID) stay direct; a design's agent relays its tools through them.

Rare follow-ups to shepherd_child_start (the profile list, a cancel): deferred under the shepherd_children namespace with shepherd_workflow; a design's agent has no tool_search, so it keeps them direct.
Standalone children report asynchronously. Continue delivery resumes the parent, report delivery stores results quietly, and workflows join dependent children. No blocking child tool or polling loop.
A scripted run of helpers: 385 tokens, the heaviest single description, for the rarest use. Deferred under the shepherd_children namespace; a design's agent has no tool_search, so it keeps it direct.
Missions are deferred and no screen shows them, so the model gets no mission tool or parameter and no record is written for a run (dropped now; SHEPHERD_MISSIONS=1 brings it back).

The thread's own Browser tabs: 17 tools, deferred together in threads and automations. Tab management and optional page targeting add no definitions to ordinary requests; loading browser tools brings in their full schemas. A design's agent has no Browser. See docs/context-budget.md for measured cost.

pi 1.0's own tool search: it loads the tools of the MCP servers left on Search (docs/mcp.md) and Shepherd's deferred tools (docs/context-budget.md, Deferred tools). 159 tokens, and the server list adds a few more while a server is on Search. Active in a thread and an automation while Defer rarely used tools is on, or an MCP server is on Search. A server set to Direct declares its own mcp__<server>__<tool> tools instead: the user's, not listed here.
Registered only once the thread holds a design reference.
Registered only while Settings > Experiments > Suggested instructions is on for the kind of agent.
What a design's agent draws, tests and edits with; no other agent gets them. board_interact exercises actual rendered state.
A design-only export step. Design launches do not provide deferred tool discovery, so keep its 166-token definition direct; it adds nothing to ordinary threads or automations.
A native subagent's only way to ask its parent; registered in a child's own pi.
